subject: Request: EU-scoped ephemeral debug-log retention carveout and SIG/CAIQ evidence
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nebulahealth.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: 2026-01-15T09:04:00-05:00
Subject: Request: EU-scoped ephemeral debug-log retention carveout and SIG/CAIQ evidence

Hi Rafael,

We're working with our privacy team to finalize production onboarding for Redwood. One outstanding ask from our DPIA and external counsel: can Redwood accommodate a customer-scoped retention window for low-level debug/troubleshooting traces generated in our EU region (examples: request-level debug logs, transient inference traces) of 14 days instead of the platform default 90 days?

Concretely, Nebula Health needs:
- Confirmation you can scope retention per-tenant/region and enforce a 14-day TTL on the debug/troubleshooting logs for our tenant in eu-west-1.
- A short evidence bundle (SIG/CAIQ mapping + SOC 2 excerpt) that documents how log deletion is implemented and how forensic preservation is handled for incidents.
- Any recommended contract language or MSA addendum we can present to legal that captures the carveout and compensating controls.

We appreciate that some logs/metrics may be necessary for platform stability; if that is the case, please call out what aggregate or derived telemetry is retained and for how long.

Can you send the evidence pack and a suggested addendum this week? Happy to set a short call if needed.

Thanks,
Liam
Director, Platform Security
Nebula Health

[Attachment: Nebula_DPIA_summary.pdf (referenced)]

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2026-01-15T13:18:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Request: EU-scoped ephemeral debug-log retention carveout and SIG/CAIQ evidence

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear ask and the DPIA excerpt. We're able to support customer-scoped retention windows; happy to outline how we'd handle the 14-day TTL for debug-level traces in your EU tenant and what stays longer for reliability.

Quick summary of next steps I propose:
1) I'll assemble a focused evidence pack (SIG/CAIQ mapping for log controls, SOC 2 excerpt highlighting log deletion procedures, and a retention matrix) and share it by EOD Thursday.
2) Kimberly (Privacy & Compliance) will propose contract language for a narrow MSA addendum that specifies the 14-day tenant-scoped TTL and the compensating controls.
3) Jordan will join to discuss operational rollout and any impact to support / pager coverage.

Couple questions to help scope the implementation:
- Which specific log classes do you want in the 14-day carveout? (e.g., request debug traces, full payload traces, model KV cache dumps, metrics/aggregates)
- Expected 90-day vs 14-day volume delta — rough daily logging volume and peak query rate for the Nebula tenant would help size removal windows and backup/retention tasks.

I'm attaching a retention matrix draft to start (redwood_retention_matrix_v1.xlsx) and will follow up with the SIG/CAIQ fragment and SOC 2 summary from compliance. If you're open, let's lock a 30-minute technical & legal sync on Friday — propose 10:30 AM CET.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_retention_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)]

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nebulahealth.com>, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2026-01-16T10:02:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Request: EU-scoped ephemeral debug-log retention carveout and SIG/CAIQ evidence

Hi Liam — looping in Compliance details here. Thank you for the clear ask; we can support a tenant-scoped 14-day TTL for transient debug/troubleshooting traces in the EU region with a documented addendum and compensating controls. Below are the high-level positions and deliverables we will provide: 

What Redwood can do now:
- Tenant/region-level TTL: We enforce object TTLs at tenant scope for debug/traces in the eu-west-1 region. Deletion is performed asynchronously but within the configured window; our baseline platform deletes eligible objects within 24–72 hours after TTL expiry.
- Evidence bundle: I will attach a SOC 2 Type II summary that highlights our deletion and change-control processes; a SIG fragment mapping the log retention controls to SIG categories; and the retention matrix Rafael attached.
- Contract language: Proposed MSA addendum clause below (draft):
  "Customer-scoped ephemeral logs: For the Nebula Health tenant deployed in EU regions, Redwood will apply a tenant-scoped Time-To-Live (TTL) of 14 days to debug and troubleshooting traces defined as non-production diagnostic traces. Redwood will implement deletion in accordance with its documented deletion workflow. Aggregated telemetry and platform health metrics required for system integrity will be retained no longer than 180 days and will be pseudonymized where feasible. In the event of a lawful preservation request or incident response, Redwood will preserve relevant data per the incident hold process and notify Customer in accordance with the Agreement."

Technical exceptions / notes:
- We cannot apply a 14-day TTL to logs required for billing, billing-adjacent auditing, and security forensics. Those classes need to be scoped explicitly.
- For forensic investigations and legal holds, TTLs are suspended for the targeted data subset until the hold is lifted. We will include the legal-hold workflow in the evidence pack.

Deliverables (attached):
- SOC2-type2-summary.pdf (excerpt highlighting log deletion controls)
- sig-log-retention-mapping.md (SIG control mapping for A.6/A.12-style categories)
- redwood_retention_matrix_v1.xlsx (retention-by-class matrix)

Next steps: please confirm the exact log classes you want in scope (short list) and whether Nebula's counsel requires the addendum to be included in your SOW or MSA. If you confirm, legal will prepare a short formal addendum for signature. We're available for the technical/legal sync Friday at 10:30 AM CET as Rafael suggested.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SOC2-type2-summary.pdf (document stub)]
[Attachment: sig-log-retention-mapping.md (markdown file stub)]

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nebulahealth.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Anya Petrov <anya.petrov@nebulahealth.com>, privacy@nebulahealth.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2026-01-20T15:30:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Request: EU-scoped ephemeral debug-log retention carveout and SIG/CAIQ evidence

Thanks Rafael and Kimberly — this is very helpful.

Scope confirmation: Nebula requests the 14-day TTL for the following classes in eu-west-1: 
- request-debug-traces (non-payload identifiers only — no PHI or full request bodies)
- model-inference-debug (model op logs that do not include raw input/output content)
- transient-kv-dumps used only for session reconstruction (we can accept redaction of raw inputs)

We understand billing, security, and audit logs are excluded. The proposed addendum language looks reasonable to present to legal; please send it as a tracked-change document.

We accept the workshop on Friday 10:30 AM CET. Agenda: quick walk through technical TTL enforcement, how deletes are verified (proof-of-delete), and the legal addendum draft. If you can include a short note on how incident holds are handled operationally, that will satisfy our counsel.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — see you Friday.

Best,
Liam
Director, Platform Security
Nebula Health
